title: Dedicated throughput negotiator and safety layer for autoscaling policies
creator: Priya Desai
description: We need an autoscaling policy engine component that translates per-tenant throughput commitments and desired latency SLOs into actionable fleet scaling targets while enforcing safety limits. This ticket proposes the 'throughput negotiator' — a control layer that composes multiple signal sources (token-rate SLA, p50/p95 latency, queued requests, KV-cache hit rate) into a single target throughput per tenant and a conservative fleet-level scale delta. The negotiator includes a safety layer with derivative caps, surge credit accounting, tier-aware headroom, and aggressive fallback rules for capacity pressure. Deliverables: spec, simulator, integration hooks into scaling loop, metrics and dashboards, and a rollout plan with kill switches.
acceptance_criteria: Spec document reviewed and signed off by Runtime, Product, and SRE
Simulator validates that negotiated targets reduce SLA breaches by >= 40% in 3 representative workload traces without >10% extra GPU hours
Integration with autoscaler control-plane and rollout flags implemented; can toggle negotiator on a per-tenant basis
Safety layer prevents scaling above configured surge budget and triggers deterministic fallback policy within 60s on persistent queue growth
End-to-end observability (per-tenant negotiated target, applied delta, reason codes) visible in Console and emission to telemetry pipeline
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Draft spec + signal composition model (2 days) — decision on weightings and default metric set
Phase 2: Build a lightweight Go simulator to replay production traces and compare baseline autoscaler vs negotiator (5 days)
Phase 3: Implement negotiator service (stateless decision API) and a small adapter in autoscaler to consume negotiated deltas (6 days)
Phase 4: Integrate safety-layer primitives (surge credit ledger, derivative cap, headroom tax) and unit/integration tests (5 days)
Phase 5: Canary rollout to staging/Dedicated beta tenants + runbooks + dashboarding (3 days)
Phase 6: Post-rollout measurement and iteration; follow-ups (sweep)
simulation_summary: Ran three representative production traces (bursting consumer workloads, steady enterprise batch, and spiky PLG) through the simulator on 2026-03-07
Negotiator reduced p95 latency violations by 46% on bursty trace compared to baseline conservative autoscaler; GPU-hours increased by 7% in that trace
For steady batch workloads negotiated targets matched baseline within 2% and did not cause unnecessary scale-ups
Surge credit mechanism prevented >90% of oscillations in the simulated emergency burst window by enforcing a per-tenant surge budget and time-decay
design_decisions: Use a small set of canonical signals: token_rate_target, p95_latency, queue_depth, kv_cache_hit_rate — extendable via DSL (deferred)
Compose signals with a weighted max-scaling heuristic (weights defaulted by tier) — avoids pathological under-provisioning vs naive averaging
Enforce a derivative cap (max delta per minute) and an absolute cap bound by surge credits to limit cost impact
Provide deterministic fallback: if queue_depth > threshold for >60s, reduce negotiated targets and open throttling path; alert SRE
Expose reason codes and contributing signals in telemetry for post-mortem and model tuning
open_questions: What should the default weight matrix be for free-tier vs enterprise tenants? (Product input required)
How to price surge credits for Dedicated customers that want guaranteed throughput but unpredictable bursts?
Should the negotiator be stateful to track long-lived surge credits, or keep state in the autoscaler (operational complexity tradeoff)?
Tolerance for small SLA regressions during canary: what is acceptable by Product and Sales teams?
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Negotiator over-provisions leading to cost blowouts — Mitigation: derivative cap + surge credit ledger + rollout feature flag per-tenant
Risk: Increased complexity in debugging scaling incidents — Mitigation: add reason codes and per-decision traces to Console; require change review and runbook
Risk: Interaction with Dedicated quota/committed capacity policies causing contention — Mitigation: admission controller in negotiator that respects committed capacity and enforces tenant priorities
Risk: Latency in decision loop (network/API) — Mitigation: colocate negotiator decision instance near autoscaler; keep decision path < 50ms median
observability_requirements: Emit negotiated_target and applied_delta per tenant per decision (1m granularity) to telemetry
Emit reason_codes and contributing_signal_values for each decision
Dashboard: negotiated targets vs observed throughput, queue depth, latency SLO breaches, allocated GPUs
Alert: sliding-window ratio of queued requests to negotiated target > 2 for > 2 minutes
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Feature flag gated in staging — run workloads and compare against baseline (1 week)
Stage 1: Canary on 5 non-critical Dedicated tenants with monitoring and automatic rollback triggers (3 days)
Stage 2: Expand to 25% of Dedicated fleet if metrics stable (1 week)
Stage 3: Full rollout to all Dedicated tenants with communication to customers and support playbook
